title.narrative: AWESOME (Advancing Women's Engagement: Strengthening Opportunities to Mobilise for Equality)

description.narrative: A 5 year advocacy programme to support women's movements in Ethiopia, Kenya and Uganda to be strengthened, less fragmented and more representative of diverse groups of women, including women and girls with disabilities. These stronger women's movements will contribute to strong women leaders at all levels, and the prevention and elimination of sexual and gender based violence(SGBV) against women and girls.

title.narrative: An increase in gender sensitive and disability inclusive coverage and reporting in the media.

description.narrative: Society 2.2: Evidence of voices of WwDs included in media and campaigns through gender/disability sensitive articles published at national and international level

comment.narrative: Limited capacity on disability issue in regards to WwDs among media personnel. Most media present WwDs as objects of pity, are rarely seen, and rarely portrayed as persons with opinions on news beyond disabiltiy topics. The journalists treat gender and disability stories as hard to sell. Yet the industry could play a central role in attitude and policy change.

Year 1: 8 media engagements ( 2 national). WCC created awareness to members of society in women with disabilities participation in leadership and matters SGBV. 7 broadcast (TV and Radio) and 1 short piece in the 'Star' newspaper which is a national paper. Through activities in AWESOME program media was interested to cover what we are doing; We also increased knowledge of media personnel on disability inclusion.Year 2: 5 national. Women with disabilities participated in media engagements including radio talk shows,tv shows and newspaper articles. These were both local and national level. We had 5 WwDs participating in radio,4 in TV and 1 in newspaper. These incorporated 4 Radio engagements,2 TV and 2 newspaper articles. Topics in discussion were rights and issues of WwDs around SGBV and women participation in leadership. WCC has noticed that media currently now engages women with disabilities in discussion on disability inclusion . Media has become more sensitive on handling disability issuesWCC trained 20 journalists from various media houses at national and local stations both television and radio. Positive change of attitudes towards women with disabilities, reporting positive stories about women with disabilities, women being invited to participate in discussion on disability inclusion and other topics of interest in the country. In Siaya one member has been granted slots once a week to appear on radio and discuss issues, in Kajiado, in Kakamega, and in Kisumu. The trainings contributed to the project through improved support from the society, enhanced knowledge of WwDs, stakeholders on peace, co-existence, rights, improved networking and recognition

We want to increase the number of disability sensitive articles published ("disability sensitive" articles means articles that have a scope of disability). All 10 articles will be national. We also want journalists to have increased knoweldge on disability inclusion. Also, we want journalist to support WwDs with political aspiration by helping in their visibility

title.narrative: An increase in the number and diversity of women supported with training, awareness raising, and networking
Number of women supported with training, awareness raising, and networking.

description.narrative: Self 1.4: # women with disabilities mobilized around their rights and Civic Education.

comment.narrative: Our baseline recorded the need for Awareness Raising and Civic Education training for WwDs. WwDs identified barriers of knowledge of all of their rights, confidence, and ability to organize for a campaign or advocacy. In addition, WwDs are not able to make a distinction between their rights as persons with disabilities and their rights as women. The WwDs will be mobilized around their disability rights, electoral rights, general knowledge of their rights as citizens of Kenya, rights in terms getting justice in case of violence. Civic education focuses mainly on role of WwDs participation in decision making processes e.g budgetary processes;civic education also touches on governance,participation in political leadership e.t.c. The targeted Women with Disabilities are existing members and new ones who are not necessarily WCC members; they are leaders of Persons with Disability Organizations, they are friends of WCC who have helped in implementation of other projects; they are also WwDs organizations or individuals we have been referred to by partners.

800 women will be mobilised in year 1, and then reached multiple times through activities in years 1-5. The WwDs will be mobilized around their disability rights, electoral rights, general knowledge of their rights as citizens of Kenya, rights in terms getting justice in case of violence. Civic education focuses mainly on role of WwDs participation in decision making processes e.g. budgetary processes; civic education also touches on governance, participation in political leadership e.t.c.

755 women + 250 men. 755 WWDs in total: 750 WwDs from civic education and awareness raising meetings; plus 5 WwDs from multi-sectoral training. Note: Not included in this number are 102 WWDs from legal clinics and 40 WwD paralegals, because we cannot be sure of double-counting with other activities; and 40 Resource Persons are already included within the 750 WwD number).Participants' knowledge of their rights was made, their role in decision making processes, the importance for them engaging meaningfully in women movements. We measured the level of increase in knowledge by finding out expectations before training and evaluation at the end of training. We also measured this by asking questions in regard to training content and having one-on-one conversations with participants during breaks.We wanted to ensure we have representation of men in our meetings so that we are not talking to ourselves. We will reduce the number of men in the coming year to ensure we meet the target of WwDs.We are targeting 800 Wwds, the remaining will be 100 men with/without disabilities and 100 women without disabilities.We will continue with the target of 1000 people overall.

In this period we have more WwDs aware of their rights and voice unifies and strenthened to collectively demand for these rights. We have achieved this through activities like community drama, legal clinics,multi-sectoral trainings and SGBV trainings. From the FGds conducted in 10 Counties,a majority of the WwDs said they feel more empowered to speak up and demand for their rights without fear. 72 WwDs took part in the FGDs. Other than the FGDs, we reached 245 new WwDs through the actitivities mentioned above.Having said these, total number of WwDs reached (both new and old/repeat participants) are 369(297+72 from FGDs).From these trainings WwDs have acquired increased level of knowledge on their role in preventing and responding to violence and their rights in accessing quality SGBV services. WwDs are demonstrating increased level of confidence in demanding their rights in spaces where they feel discriminated e.g. when they go to seek services in hospitals or government institutions. Further, as a result of increased knowledge, WwDs are not passive but they are going ahead to pass what they have learnt to other WwDs whom we have not reached especially those in very remote areas.

WCC was able to engage 605 new women with disabilities to be mobilized around their rights and civic education. This is additional to the 1005 that were engaged in Year 1. The women participated in awareness of and civic education training, mutlt-sectoral and community drama training, legal clinics, and SGBV training. This resulted in more women being aware of their rights and there were follow up sessions with these women as well. These women had increased capacities in leadership due to the trainings, as well as stakeholders knowledge on disability inclusion. There was also more acceptance and focus on initiatives of women with disabilities. These initiatives and trainings congribute to the goal of working towards improving the quality of lives of these WwDs , better networking within stronger feminism movements of both mainstream WROs and organizations of WwDs, increased recognition by the society. WCC was able to support the mobilization of a high number of additional women with disabilities because of they offered various different types of actvities in addition to the awraness raising and trainning sessions for WwDs to paritipcate and engage in as previously stated (ex. legal clinics,SGBV training, and community dramas). WCC was able to reach an additional 605 women than the target 800 because they reached additional counties (Vihiga, Nakuru, Mombasa, Kajiado, Baringo, Garissa, and Nairobi Counties) which were not included and reached in Y1, and no budget adjustments need to be made and this additional reach was incorporated into work plans and budget in preparation for Y2.

We have increased knowledge and skills of 68 new WwD on their rights when preventing and responding to GBV, matrimonial and inheritance rights, reproductive health rights, right to participate in leadership and electoral processes, enhancing knowledge on their rights, increase capacity pathways to access to justice through community drama and media engagements. We are able to measure these changes through focus group discussions, discussions before and after training.
